title: Append selected ideal generators to a residue differential basis
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], and let $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ be prime. Put $L=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $F/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], with a $k$-algebra embedding $\iota:F\to K$. Fix $t,r\ge0$, elements $x_j\in\Lambda$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}(t)$), elements $y_i\in\mathfrak q$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$) whose images generate $\mathfrak qL$, and elements $a_j\in F$ such that $\iota(a_j)$ is the residue of $x_j/1$. Assume $(\mathrm da_j)_j$ is an $F$-basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then there exist $e\ge0$ and $s:\operatorname{Fin}(e)\to\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ such that the explicitly defined polynomial map $\varphi:k[X_1,\ldots,X_{t+e}]\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], sending its first $t$ variables to $x_j$ and its last $e$ variables to $y_{s(i)}$, extends to a ring map $\psi:k[X_1,\ldots,X_{t+e}]_{\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)}\to L$. This map restricts to the composite of $\varphi$ and $\Lambda\to L$, is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and satisfies $\mathfrak qL=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)L$. No subalgebra of a thickened quotient, containment, or differential-spanning conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: Put L = Λ_q and K = κ(q). L is Noetherian, and geometrically regular over k: after each finite purely inseparable scalar extension, L is a localization of the corresponding scalar extension of Λ, which is regular. Base change of localization and preservation of regularity prove this.

Identify F with the image of its k-algebra embedding ι into K; field homomorphisms are injective. Essential finite type for a field extension is finite generation as a field (Mathlib IntermediateField.fg_top_iff), and this property and the given differential basis transport across the field algebra isomorphism. The polynomial map xs has exactly the prescribed residues ha. Apply lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-over-field-flat to L, this image field and this basis. The first localized polynomial map is flat and its closed fibre S is regular local. The prime used there equals the contraction of q because qL contracts to q.

The given ys generate qL, so their images generate the maximal ideal of S. Extract from their cotangent images a basis; its lifts are a subset indexed by s : Fin e → Fin r. Nakayama shows that they generate that maximal ideal. The basis size e is the embedding dimension, hence dim S, so the selected images form a regular system of parameters and, by lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence, a regular sequence. This also permits the empty sequence when S is a field.

Define φ by evaluating the first t variables at xs and the last e at ys ∘ s, exactly Fin.addCases in Lean. Extend it to ψ by localization, since the complement of q.comap φ maps to units of L. Its restriction is the required composite. The extended contracted prime lies inside qL; it contains the first-coordinate ideal and the selected parameters, whose sum is qL by their generation of the maximal ideal of S. This gives the ideal equality.

The closed fibre of the extended polynomial localization over the first polynomial localization is the polynomial ring on e variables over κ(p′), localized at the origin. Indeed the contracted prime contains all added variables, and their ideal in this fibre is already maximal. By lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-origin-regular-local its localization is regular local of dimension e with these variables as parameters. Both polynomial localizations are Noetherian local and the induced maps are local.

The map of closed fibres sends the e parameters to the selected regular sequence in S; the quotient is its nonzero residue field. Apply lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular to obtain fibre flatness. Apply lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian to the first polynomial localization, the extended localization, and L as a module over itself. Initial flatness comes from the second step, and L is finite and nonzero over itself. It follows that ψ is flat.

theorem exists_popescu_append_flat_parameters
    (k : Type u) (Λ : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (hreg : IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ) (q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime]
    (F : Type w) [Field F] [Algebra k F] [EssFiniteType k F]
    (ι : F →ₐ[k] q.ResidueField)
    (t r : ℕ) (xs : Fin t → Λ) (ys : Fin r → Λ) (a : Fin t → F)
    (ha : ∀ j, ι (a j) = IsLocalRing.residue (Localization.AtPrime q)
      (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (xs j)))
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin t) F (KaehlerDifferential k F))
    (hb : ∀ j, b j = KaehlerDifferential.D k F (a j))
    (hyq : ∀ i, ys i ∈ q)
    (hys : Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (ys i))) =
      q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) :
    ∃ (e : ℕ) (s : Fin e → Fin r),
      let φ : MvPolynomial (Fin (t + e)) k →ₐ[k] Λ :=
        MvPolynomial.aeval (Fin.addCases xs (fun i ↦ ys (s i)))
      ∃ ψ : Localization.AtPrime (q.comap φ.toRingHom) →+* Localization.AtPrime q,
        ψ.comp (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin (t + e)) k)
            (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap φ.toRingHom))) =
          (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp φ.toRingHom ∧
        q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) =
          (q.comap φ.toRingHom).map
            ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp φ.toRingHom) ∧
        ψ.Flat
